What About Dietary Cholesterol? 
Dietary cholesterol also has a small impact on overall blood cholesterol levels, but not as much as 
some people may think. For most people, decreasing dietary cholesterol intake has little impact on 
blood cholesterol, because their bodies respond to dietary cholesterol intake by reducing synthesis 
of cholesterol in favor of using the cholesterol obtained from food. Genetic factors may also influence 
the way a person’s body responds to changes in cholesterol intake. The 2015 U.S. Dietary Guidelines 
for Americans (DGA) suggest limiting saturated fats, thereby indirectly limiting dietary cholesterol 
since foods that are high in cholesterol tend to also be high in saturated fats. (Eggs and fish are 
notable exceptions; both are high in cholesterol but low in saturated fats.)
